cases.arabic: أسعد بن زرارة ذكر في الذي قبله إن ثبت وسيأتي في ترجمة عبد الله بن أسعد بن زرارة أن بعضهم روى الحديث المذكور في ترجمته فقال عن عبد الله بن أسعد بن زرارة عن أبيه فلعله كان فيه بن أسعد قال وهو عبد الله هذا

candidates.bodyEnglish: Mentioned in the preceding [one], if established; and it will come in the biography of 'Abd Allah bin As'ad bin Zurarah that some of them narrated the hadith mentioned in his biography, saying: from 'Abd Allah bin As'ad bin Zurarah, from his father; so perhaps in it [the name] was bin As'ad. He said: and this is this 'Abd Allah.

He was mentioned in the preceding entry, if that is established. It will be stated in the entry on ʿAbd Allāh ibn Asʿad ibn Zurāra that some transmitted the hadith mentioned in his entry, saying, “From ʿAbd Allāh ibn Asʿad ibn Zurāra, from his father.” Perhaps it contained the words “ibn Asʿad.” He said, “And it is this ʿAbd Allāh.”
issues: In the opening phrase “if that is established,” the source leaves the referent unstated.
The speaker of the final “He said” is not identified in the source.

cases.arabic: جرول بن الأحنف بن السمط بن امرئ القيس بن عمرو بن معاوية بن الحارث الأكبر الكندي قيل هو اسم جد رجاء بن حيوة قاله أحمد بن محمد بن الحجاج بن رشدين وروى الطبراني من طريق جارية بن مصعب عن رجاء بن حيوة عن أبيه عن جده وهو من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن جارية من سبي حنين مرت بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال لمن هذه الحديث ولم يسم جده وحكى بن عساكر فيه قولين آخرين أحدهما جندل بنون ثم دال والآخر بزاي بدل الدال

candidates.bodyEnglish: It is said he is the name of the grandfather of Raja' bin Haywa; said by Ahmad bin Muhammad bin al-Hajjaj bin Rushdin. And al-Tabarani narrated via the route of Jariya bin Mus'ab from Raja' bin Haywa from his father from his grandfather, and he is among the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, [narrating] that a captive from the spoils of Hunayn passed by the Prophet ﷺ, and he said, "Whose is this?" [the Hadith], and he did not name his grandfather. And Ibn 'Asakir reported two other opinions regarding him: one of them is Jandal with a nun then a dal, and the other is with a zay instead of the dal.
candidates.titleEnglish: Jarwal bin al-Ahnaf bin al-Samt bin Imru' al-Qays bin 'Amr bin Mu'awiya bin al-Harith al-Akbar al-Kindi

candidates.bodyEnglish: It is said that this was the name of the grandfather of Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa. Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥajjāj ibn Rushdayn said this. Al-Ṭabarānī transmitted, by way of Jāriya ibn Muṣʿab, from Rajāʾ ibn Ḥaywa, from his father, from his grandfather—and he was one of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ—that a slave girl from among the captives of Ḥunayn passed by the Prophet ﷺ, and he said, “To whom does this belong?”—the hadith. His grandfather was not named. Ibn ʿAsākir related two other opinions concerning the name: one was Jandal, with a nūn followed by a dāl, and the other had a zāy in place of the dāl.
issues: The grandfather in the chain is explicitly left unnamed.
The expression “the hadith” marks an omitted continuation of the report.
The source gives competing spellings of the grandfather’s name.
candidates.titleEnglish: Jarwal ibn al-Aḥnaf ibn al-Simṭ ibn Imruʾ al-Qays ibn ʿAmr ibn Muʿāwiya ibn al-Ḥārith al-Akbar al-Kindī

cases.arabic: الحارث بن فروة بن الشيطان بن خديج بن امرئ القيس بن الحارث بن معاوية بن الحارث بن معاوية بن ثور الكندي ذكر بن الكلبي وابن سعد والطبري أن له وفادة وقال بن الأثير وقع في ذيل أبي موسى الحارث بن قرة بقاف والذي في الجمهرة فروة بفاء وزيادة واو وهو الصواب وقال إن جده الشيطان سمي بذلك لجماله

candidates.bodyEnglish: Ibn al-Kalbi, Ibn Sa'd, and al-Tabari mentioned that he had a delegation. And Ibn al-Athir said: In the Dhayl Abi Musa, [it is] al-Harith bin Qarra with a Qaf, and that which is in al-Jamhara is Farwa with a Fa' and an additional Waw, and that is the correct [version]. And [he] said that his grandfather al-Shaytan was named so because of his beauty.
candidates.titleEnglish: Al-Harith bin Farwa bin al-Shaytan bin Khadij bin Imru' al-Qays bin al-Harith bin Mu'awiya bin al-Harith bin Mu'awiya bin Thawr al-Kindi

candidates.bodyEnglish: Ibn al-Kalbī, Ibn Saʿd, and al-Ṭabarī mentioned that he made a deputation visit. Ibn al-Athīr said that the name occurring in the Supplement of Abū Mūsā is “al-Ḥārith ibn Qurra,” with a qāf, whereas the form in the Jamharah is “Farwa,” with a fāʾ and an additional wāw, and that this is correct. He said that his ancestor al-Shayṭān was so named because of his beauty.
issues: The destination and circumstances of the deputation visit are not stated.
candidates.titleEnglish: Al-Ḥārith ibn Farwa ibn al-Shayṭān ibn Khudayj ibn Imruʾ al-Qays ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Muʿāwiya ibn al-Ḥārith ibn Muʿāwiya ibn Thawr al-Kindī
